task: land a meeting time with another person through a scheduling tool (Calendly, Doodle, Microsoft Bookings): open the invite link — or set up the event/poll and get it answered — compare availability, pick a slot, confirm; complete when the meeting-confirmed screen, or the poll's agreed final time, is on screen with the event details. Either side of the handshake belongs as long as the recording reaches a confirmed time. Surface pinned: a scheduling tool on the web. Variants: emailing back and forth about times, plain calendar-event creation with no counterparty, and configuring availability settings without a resulting booking do not belong.

tree.label: Schedule a meeting with others
tree.note: do 1. 2, 3, 4 in the order the tool's wizard dictates - Doodle and Outlook describe first (eZyb, W0fS), Google Calendar sets the rules first and takes the description on page two (VKIQ); 5.1 comes before 3 in the mail family, because the poll pane stays disabled until someone is on the To line and the availability icons need those names (VxrV, KbIz). then 5. 6 happens on the other side of the link - nine keepers cross over, always by simulating the invitee. 7 on poll routes only: booking routes commit at 6.5.4, and when2meet stops at the heatmap with no close at all (ythO). 8 interleaves from the first committed change - holds are checked minutes after sending (VxrV), rule edits are checked by refreshing the public page mid-setup (6Pzf). 9 when the offer needs editing and re-sharing, or taking down.

children.label: Get into the scheduling tool
children.note: 1.1 and 1.2 on web arrivals from search (udxi, X48l, 6Yg3); 1.3 once, on the desktop add-in (KbIz). 1.4 as the account state demands - most keepers arrive signed in, one goes guest, one registers from nothing, and Doodle lets creation start first and injects the wall mid-flow (MVu8, udxi). 1.5 whenever a nag interrupts. then 1.6 and 1.7; 1.8 where a first run offers it (VKIQ).

questions.check: What does the location field show?

questions.check: Which video tools does the page offer, and which one shows as connected?

questions.check: What does the start-time increment setting show?

questions.why: Creating a calendar event for a task like the 'Revision to YT Script' automatically removes that time slot from your scheduling page so others cannot book it.

questions.check: Does the page say calendar events remove matching times from the booking page?

questions.check: What does the duration field show?
questions.say_example: Set it to <60 minutes>, like you asked.

questions.question: Do you need to change the default time zone?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that the scheduling tool has correctly detected and applied your local time zone.
questions.check: What time zone does the page say it is using, and does it match the person's time zone?
questions.say_example: The page was showing everything in <Eastern>. You're on <Pacific>, so I switched it. Every time you hear from me is in your time zone.

children.label: Set the availability rules
children.note: 3.4.1 and 3.4.2, then 3.4.3 to 3.4.8 in the order the accordion presents them - the corpus sweeps every section and demo-toggles as it goes (VKIQ). LDkn touches only 3.4.1 and 3.4.3; 6Pzf only 3.4.3 and 3.4.5.

questions.question: Do you want this booking schedule to run indefinitely, or should it have a specific end date?

questions.why: Organizers often require specific qualifying information. If the agent skips these custom fields, the form will reject the submission with a validation error.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might assume the booking succeeded or get stuck on the form without knowing how to provide the missing contextual information.
questions.check: Does the form show a validation error naming the blank required field?
questions.say_example: The form won't book without <a phone number>, and I don't have one from you. What should I put?

questions.question: Does the confirmation screen state that the meeting is fully booked, or does it say the request is pending the organizer's approval?
questions.why: Some booking pages are configured to require manual approval. If it's only a request, you cannot assume the time is locked in and must watch for a follow-up confirmation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might report the meeting as confirmed and block your calendar, even though the organizer might reject the request and propose a different time.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say confirmed, or does it say pending approval?
questions.say_example: Heads up - this isn't booked yet. The page says it's a request, and <the host> still has to approve it. I'll watch for the real confirmation.

questions.question: Did a temporary success banner or 'toast' notification appear on screen to confirm the booking before vanishing?
questions.why: Success confirmations are sometimes transient visual banners that disappear automatically after a few seconds, rather than resolving to a persistent confirmation page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses definitive proof that the booking was successfully processed if the agent fails to capture the fleeting visual confirmation.
questions.check: Did a success confirmation appear - as a banner or a page - and what did it say?
questions.say_example: Caught the success banner before it vanished and saved what it said for the report.

children.label: Close the poll
children.note: poll routes only - booking routes commit inside 6.5, and when2meet never closes (ythO ends at the heatmap, the choosing left outside the tool). 7.1 and 7.2 repeat as votes land. then one of 7.3 (consensus fires on its own) or 7.4 with 7.5 (the organizer forces it - because consensus failed (W0fS) or was switched off (KbIz), or because Doodle's close is always manual (M5A9, MVu8)). 7.6 where the result gets announced - two keepers decline the built-in version for Gmail.

questions.question: Do you have all the required votes to finalize the meeting time, or should you view the full poll first?
questions.why: The email summary showed missing votes for some attendees, making it necessary to check the full poll rather than immediately clicking an inline schedule button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that all required attendees have provided their availability before the meeting time is locked in.
questions.check: Does the email summary show votes still missing, and does the full poll page list every response?
questions.say_example: The email showed votes missing, so I opened the full poll before trusting it.

questions.question: Who submitted a new vote on your poll and what were their choices?
questions.why: Reviewing the email notification showing Nestor Wilke's vote details allows you to track individual availability for the proposed times.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the context of individual attendee preferences and the ability to monitor the poll's progress directly from their inbox.
questions.check: What does the notification show - who voted, and for which times?
questions.say_example: <Name> voted: yes to <Monday>, no to the rest.

questions.question: Do you rely on the email's partial voting summary to pick a time, or do you click 'View poll' to evaluate all responses on the website?
questions.why: The email states the poll did not reach consensus but shows two positive votes for Monday at 8:30 AM, prompting a choice between trusting the summary or investigating the full details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the nuanced voting preferences and manually decide which proposed time is the best compromise.
questions.check: Does the poll page show responses the email summary does not?
questions.say_example: Read the full poll page, not the email summary - the email only carries some of the votes.

questions.question: Does the vote count in the notification email reconcile with the total attendees and the votes cast so far?
questions.why: The notification email stating '2 votes of 6' must correctly reflect the 6 total attendees listed earlier and the two votes cast by the organizer and Nestor.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the scheduling tool accurately tracked all required and optional attendees' responses.
questions.check: Does the vote count in the email match the count shown on the poll page?
questions.say_example: The email says <2 of 6> voted but the poll page shows <3>. I'm going by the poll page - the email is behind.

questions.question: Which attendees voted 'Prefer' and which voted 'Yes' for each proposed slot?
questions.why: The screen shows a detailed breakdown of attendee votes, such as 'Prefer' or 'Yes', and provides options to finalize the meeting for specific time slots.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to manually weigh individual attendee preferences and make a nuanced decision on which time slot to finalize.
questions.check: What does the vote grid show for each time - who said prefer, yes, or no?
questions.say_example: Read the grid person by person before picking anything.

questions.question: Which time slots does the group calendar's color scale show as most available, from white for nobody free to dark green for everybody free?
questions.why: The legend showing '0/2 Available' as white and '2/2 Available' as dark green helps you quickly identify the time slots that work for the most people.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate visual intuition of the calendar's heat map to quickly gauge the group's overall availability patterns.
questions.check: What does the legend say each color means?
questions.say_example: Dark green is everyone free - the legend spells it out, so I ranked times by it.

questions.question: Did the poll reach a consensus and when is the meeting scheduled?
questions.why: The email shows that the poll reached a consensus and lists the finalized meeting time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the opportunity to personally review the consensus email and verify the final meeting details.
questions.check: Does the notification say consensus was reached, and for which time?
questions.say_example: Everyone answered, and <Tuesday at 10> works for all of them. Next step is booking it - I'll check with you there.

questions.question: Which proposed time slot should you select to finalize the meeting based on the poll responses?
questions.why: Reviewing the vote status icons ensures you choose a time slot that has the most favorable responses from all participants.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally weigh the participants' specific preferences when deciding the final meeting time.
questions.check: What do the vote tallies show for each proposed time?
questions.say_example: <4 of 5> can make <Tuesday at 10> - everyone but <name>. Booking it sends invites to the whole list. Book it, wait for more votes, or pick another time?

questions.question: What does the 'Poll saved!' dialog confirm was saved, read out before it is dismissed?
questions.why: Dismissing the success message clears the screen so you can review the final agreed-upon meeting details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing the success message confirming your changes were saved.
questions.check: Does a saved confirmation dialog block the page?
questions.say_example: Closed the saved box to get back to the details.

questions.question: How should you share the final poll results with the participants?
questions.why: The screen provides built-in link and email sharing options for the closed poll, but using the platform's automated system risks the notification being caught in spam filters.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the deliverability assurance of sending a separate, direct email from their own account rather than relying on the scheduling tool's automated sharing.
questions.check: Which share options does the closed poll show?
questions.say_example: Sent the result through the site's own share. If anyone says nothing arrived, spam is the first place to look.

questions.question: Did you notify the participants of the final date after closing the poll?
questions.why: The video ends after the poll is closed at 10:39 without showing any message being sent to participants with the final result.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that participants are informed of the final meeting time, potentially leading to missed meetings.
questions.check: Does the page or the sent mail show the final time was shared with the participants?
questions.say_example: The poll is closed but nobody was told the result yet. Everyone who voted is still guessing. Sending the final time now.

questions.question: Did you include the necessary video conferencing link in the final confirmation message?
questions.why: Because the free tier of the scheduling tool may not automatically generate or allow clickable links in the location field, you must manually paste the meeting link into the message body before sending the final results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks sending a finalized meeting confirmation that lacks the actual meeting link, causing confusion and requiring a follow-up email.
questions.check: Does the final message text contain a joinable meeting link, not just a location word?
questions.say_example: The final invite says <Zoom> but carries no actual link - on the free plan the location line can't hold one. Pasted the real link into the message.

questions.question: Should you send the final meeting confirmation to everyone originally invited, or only to those who actually participated in the poll?
questions.why: The 'Share results' email dialog provides quick-select options for 'Participated' and 'Everyone', forcing a decision on whether non-respondents should still receive the final meeting details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to exclude unresponsive invitees from the final meeting or, conversely, ensure that key people who forgot to vote are still informed of the scheduled time.
questions.check: Which recipient option is selected - participated, or everyone?
questions.say_example: Sent it to everyone invited. The ones who never voted still need to know it's happening.

children.label: Verify across the surfaces
children.note: runs throughout, not after: 8.2 minutes after sending (VxrV), 8.5 after any rule edit, mid-setup included (6Pzf, VKIQ). 8.1 to 8.4 after any commit, on whichever of the two to four surfaces the keeper trusts; 8.6 when a vote seems missing (udxi); 8.7 against everything the setup promised.

questions.question: Does a meeting with this person already exist before this one is booked?
questions.why: The inbox at 04:27 shows a meeting confirmation received at 2:52 PM, making the subsequent booking flow completed at 05:25 chronologically impossible.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user receives a fabricated or out-of-order execution record instead of a genuine, chronological scheduling process.
questions.check: Does the inbox already show a confirmation for a meeting with this person around this time?
questions.say_example: Your inbox already has a confirmation for a meeting with <name> on <date>. Booking again would double it. Still want me to?

questions.question: Are the tentative holds for the proposed meeting times appearing correctly on your calendar?
questions.why: Checking the calendar holds ensures that the proposed times were successfully blocked off to prevent double-booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visual reassurance that their calendar correctly reflects the tentative holds for the proposed meeting.
questions.check: Does the calendar show a hold for each offered time?
questions.say_example: The holds never landed on your calendar. The offered times look free to anyone booking you, so I'm watching those slots by hand until the poll closes.

questions.question: Is the meeting scheduled, and at what time?
questions.why: The screen showed a voting page with a confirmation message, making it essential to confirm the final status of the invite.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that the meeting was actually finalized and added to the calendar.
questions.check: Does the page show the meeting as scheduled, with its final time?
questions.say_example: Done. <Tuesday at 10> is booked, everyone got the invite, and it's on your calendar.

questions.question: Are the temporary holds removed and the final meeting correctly placed on your calendar?
questions.why: The calendar shows a single meeting block for 'Trade Show - 2023' at 9:30 AM, confirming the previous holds are gone.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The peace of mind of visually confirming your calendar is clean and the meeting is accurately scheduled.
questions.check: Does the calendar show only the final event, with no leftover holds?
questions.say_example: Two old holds are still sitting on your calendar from the poll. They'd block real bookings, so I'm clearing them.

questions.question: Are the meeting details, attendees, and Teams link correct in the final calendar event?
questions.why: Verifying the title, attendees, times, and the Teams link ensures the meeting was scheduled exactly as intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that the correct people and meeting link are included in the final invite.
questions.check: Do the event's title, time, duration, attendee list, and join link match what was approved?
questions.say_example: The booked event runs <45 minutes>, not the <30> you approved. Fixing it before anyone plans around the wrong block.

questions.question: Did the setting change apply correctly to the live booking page?
questions.why: Refreshing the page to verify that only the next four days are available on the December 2024 calendar confirms your scheduling constraints are active before picking a date.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to visually verify that your custom availability rules are correctly restricting the options shown to guests.
questions.check: After a refresh, does the public page reflect the changed setting?
questions.say_example: The change didn't reach the live page - it still offers <all 30 days>. Re-saving before anyone books off the stale version.

questions.question: The participant view showed only a loading spinner - did the added time slots actually render for participants?
questions.why: The screen shows a blank page with a Doodle loading spinner instead of the expected poll details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to confirm that the new time slots were successfully added and are visible to participants.
questions.check: Does the page show content, or still a loading spinner?
questions.say_example: The participant view hung on its spinner. Reloaded and read it again - I don't report from a blank page.

questions.question: Do the available booking slots accurately exclude all times that would overlap with the newly created busy event?
questions.why: The screen needs to confirm whether a 30-minute slot at 1:50pm actually remains available despite a busy event starting at 2:00pm.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses a conflict-free schedule if the agent books an appointment that overlaps with an existing busy block.
questions.check: Does any offered slot overlap a time the calendar shows as busy?
questions.say_example: The page still offers <1:50>, but you're busy at <2>. The slot runs past it - pulling it before someone books it.

questions.question: Are the newly added time slots visible on the poll, and which one should you select?
questions.why: Confirming that the three new options for August 5th are visible ensures the poll updated correctly before you commit to a specific time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify the poll updated correctly and to personally choose your preferred time from the new options.
questions.check: Does the live poll show the newly added times?
questions.say_example: The times I added aren't showing on the live poll yet. Not sending anyone there until they appear.

questions.question: Does the copied link work and display the correct event information to your participants?
questions.why: Verifying that the loaded page shows the correct event title, duration, and availabilities ensures the poll was set up properly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind that comes from visually confirming exactly what your invitees will see when they open the link.
questions.check: Does the copied link load a page whose title, duration, and times match the created event?
questions.say_example: The copied link opens the wrong thing - it shows <another event>. Re-copying the right one before it goes out.

questions.question: Is your newly booked time slot now missing from the public booking page?
questions.why: The available times for Thursday the 13th skip from 1:50pm to 3:10pm, confirming that the 2:30pm slot was successfully blocked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their booking actually updated the public calendar to prevent double-booking.
questions.check: Is the just-booked time still offered on the public page?
questions.say_example: The slot you just booked still shows as open to others. Until it drops off, someone could double-book it - watching it.

questions.question: The dashboard reads 'No participants yet' - is that the current vote state or a stale page that has not refetched?
questions.why: The 'Availabilities' section displays 'No participants yet' because the page state is stale and hasn't automatically fetched the latest votes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the intuition to manually refresh the browser when expected updates fail to appear automatically.
questions.check: Does the page show no participants, and does a refresh change it?
questions.say_example: The dashboard said no participants until a refresh - it doesn't update itself.

questions.question: Does the availabilities table show the vote you submitted?
questions.why: Checking the availabilities table ensures your name and selected times, such as the highlighted 3:45 PM slot, were successfully recorded by the system.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that your specific availability was correctly captured in the group's poll.
questions.check: Does the availabilities table list the person's name with the times they picked?
questions.say_example: Your vote isn't in the table - the <3:45> you picked shows empty. Submitting it again and checking the table after.

questions.question: The premium trial was reported active, but a later screen warns that only premium users can add links - is the account actually on premium before the poll depends on it?

questions.check: Do any pages show premium features as locked?

questions.question: Do the generated time slots correctly reflect your adjusted availability window, duration, and buffer?
questions.why: The screen showed exactly six slots from 9:00am to 12:20pm, confirming that the 30-minute duration and 10-minute buffer were correctly applied to the 9:00am to 1:00pm window.

questions.question: Does the selected slot still leave the configured buffer around it?
questions.why: The 'Enter Details' page displays the selected event time of 10:30am - 11:15am, which dictates when any configured buffer periods will apply.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify that the selected time slot correctly accommodates their required buffer before finalizing the booking.
questions.check: What time range does the page show for the selected appointment?
questions.say_example: Booked <10:30 to 11:15>; the buffer pads your calendar after it.

questions.question: Do the emojis in the published poll description exactly match the ones from the AI suggestion?
questions.why: Comparing the published poll to the initial setup ensures the platform didn't alter your intended text or emojis upon submission.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the guarantee that their exact intended message and tone were preserved without silent modifications by the platform.
questions.check: Does the published description text match what was entered?
